title: Research: sharp infinite-dihedral reflection bills with arbitrary dirty registers
body:
## Result and scope

In the explicit nonabelian formal model `F2[D_infinity]`, with `D_infinity=<x,y | x^2=y^2=1>`, paid labels **only x and y**, arbitrary rank-one scalar idempotents and free scalar register mixing, diagonal targets `g_i=(xy)^k_i x^e_i` have the sharp separate paid-call bills:

- x calls: `sum |k_i+e_i|`
- y calls: `sum |k_i|`

The theorem holds for every finite register count and arbitrarily many restored dirty spectators. Direct freely reduced words attain both bounds simultaneously. Thus positive per-label tariffs give exactly `alpha sum|k_i+e_i| + beta sum|k_i|`.

The proof uses two swapped Laurent representations and Cauchy–Binet maximal-minor degree, not a bounded word census or finite-column extrapolation. The package includes the uniform full-group-algebra attaining identity, all role charges, and a concrete finite-array reflection implementation invoice. **Scoped formal-model negative theorem; no new kappa, native supplier admission or selected-frontier change.**

## Task, pins and overlap

- Task: `bit-new-register-model`, refined to the explicitly infinite dihedral alphabet and arbitrary mixed diagonal targets.
- Base: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`.
- Selected-record SHA256 unchanged: `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`.
- Source byte/blob pins: `research/infinite-dihedral-register-bound/SOURCES.json`.
- Coordination: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1884

Closest inspected predecessors are #1573 (already proves all-register finite D8 central targets), #1478 (D8, two/three registers), #1821 (D16, two registers), #1733 (four-register rational two-relation ansatz), and #1822 (Q8). Exact heads are recorded in README and were rechecked unchanged immediately before publication. This result neither claims their conclusions anew nor extends them: the Laurent representation does **not** descend to finite dihedral quotients.

An offline exact-term overlap search used the shared snapshots of 543 open PRs including drafts (2026-10-14 13:23:53Z) and 529 discussion records (13:25:07Z), with complete pagination. Only this local package matched `infinite dihedral`. Cached coverage may miss recent changes, closed work is represented through local notes/ledger only, and arbitrary diffs were not searched. No novelty guarantee is claimed.

## Verification actually performed

macOS arm64, CPython 3.12.12, standard library only:

```sh
uv run --python 3.12 --no-project scripts/research_package.py --package research/infinite-dihedral-register-bound --check-only
uv run --python 3.12 --no-project scripts/research_package.py --package research/infinite-dihedral-register-bound
uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python -I -B research/infinite-dihedral-register-bound/verify.py
```

All passed. Registered isolated optimized replay: **0.29 seconds**. Direct isolated unoptimized smoke: **0.18 seconds**. Both emitted:

```text
{"formal_targets": 102, "generator_minor_checks": 28, "mixed_words": 144, "omission_controls": 540, "other_controls": 4, "projectors": 155}
PASS_INFINITE_DIHEDRAL_REGISTER_BOUND finite_checks_only; universal_proof=README.md
```

The registered run also emitted `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed`; metadata/pins passed separately. The checker covers all projectors for R=1..4, all 144 two-call words over the two-register alphabet, independent integer-affine and literal-reduction group arithmetic, represented minor bounds, complete formal endpoints, invoices, omission/order/label/dirty-state controls, and a finite-quotient alias control. These finite checks corroborate the written theorem; they are not its universal proof.

The prescribed `research_baseline.py` source-binding positive control passed. No full repository suite or selected cold replay was run.

## Limits and next questions

No proof-assistant or independent human review is claimed. There is no native all-size bit-supplier compiler/interface mapping, hosting, precision/tape, recursive coverage or analytic transfer claim. The finite-array invoice prices the witness, not optimal finite-quotient physical execution.

Open next questions in README/TASK: a torsion-aware invariant for arbitrary-workspace finite dihedral targets, and a justified native reflection implementation with complete interface costs. Neither is silently assumed solved.
